correctness.rationale: For nonidentical Boolean tables choose a subset of differing value and give it to the agent who values it 1. If (1,1) is realizable it is immediately EF+PO; otherwise this allocation is envy-free and has (1,0) or (0,1), which is on the binary Pareto frontier. For equal valuations an identical 11 complementary pair yields (1,1); if none, all Pareto allocations with a 1/0 utility split envy the winner, except the identically zero table, which is trivially EF+PO. EF alone requires equal valuations on both bundles in some complement pair, giving the all-01/10 excluded class. The 2^m bundles partition into L complementary pairs, each with 00,01,10,11; exclude 11 for all L and remove globally zero -> 3^L-1, while no-EF forces 01/10 ->2^L. Independently exhaustively checked all 65,808 ordered truth-table pairs for m=1..3 directly from EF inequalities and PO dominance, reproducing (2,8,80) failure counts.

final_claim: For m>=1 goods, complete allocation between two agents with arbitrary (possibly nonmonotone, unnormalized) Boolean set functions is EF and Pareto optimal iff the valuations differ, or they coincide and are identically zero, or they coincide and some complementary bundles both have value 1. Thus failure iff identical nonzero functions have no complementary 11 pair. No EF iff identical valuation with each complement pair opposite bits. Under uniform independent truth-table bits L=2^(m-1), the respective failure counts are 3^L-1 and 2^L among 16^L valuation profiles.
